ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.claim: The concluding discourse returns to the sūrah's opening theme: Qur'anic warnings are true, punishment signs can come, and prophetic histories already serve as signs for the stubborn Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.anchor: Coming up are the concluding verses of the sūrah and the discourse links to its introductory part which is the real theme.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r1.claim: One reading begins the command to trust with fa; the other seven canonical readers use waw.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r2.claim: The paired names mean the One who cannot be overcome and the One who shows mercy; trust in Him defeats enemies through might and brings aid through mercy. Tawakkul entrusts affairs to their capable owner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r2.anchor: فهو يقهر أعداءك بعزته، وينصرك عليهم برحمته. والتوكل هو تفويض الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r3.claim: Tawakkul is entrusting one’s affair to someone who controls it and can bring benefit or harm.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r3.anchor: والتوكل عبارة عن تفويض الرجل أمره إلى من يملك أمره ويقدر على نفعه وضره

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r4.claim: The Mighty crushes the Prophet’s enemies by His might, and the Merciful helps him against them through His mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r4.anchor: على الذي يقهر أعداءك بعزته وينصرك عليهم برحمته

BURSEVI:v6p227/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p227/r5.claim: Entrust every state to the Almighty: He never humiliates those loyal to Him and can overpower His enemies.
BURSEVI:v6p227/r5.anchor: {وتوكل} في جميع حالاتك {على العزيز} الذي لا يذل من والاه ولا يعز من عاداه

BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r1.claim: God grants victory and support to those who rely on Him and entrust their affairs to Him, and He helps His friends.
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r1.anchor: {الرحيم} الذي يرحم من توكل عليه وفوض أمره إليه بالظفر والنصرة فهو ينصر أولياءه

BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r2.claim: God alone suffices against enemies; reliance on others should be abandoned. Turning wholly to God is a mark of the perfected.
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r2.anchor: ولا تتوكل على الغير فإن الله تعالى هو الكافي لشر الأعداء لا الغير والتوكل على الله تعالى في جميع الأمور

STUDYQURAN:26:217/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:217/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:217/r1.claim: Trust means placing all fear and hope in God; reliance of the heart grows as faith grows.
STUDYQURAN:26:217/r1.anchor: one’s fear and hope should rest entirely with God, reflecting the heart’s reliance upon God, which increases as one’s faith grows

STUDYQURAN:26:217/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:217/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:217/r2.claim: Trust in God is central to Islamic spirituality and is enjoined in many verses; the commentary also cites 14:11–12 on its significance.
STUDYQURAN:26:217/r2.anchor: believers are told in dozens of verses to trust in God

TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r2.claim: The Prophet should trust the Mighty in His punishment of enemies and the Merciful toward those who repent; the attribute is also linked to 1:1.
TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r2.anchor: في نقمته من أعدائه {الرحيم} [الفاتحة: 1] بمن أناب إليه وتاب من معاصيه.

TABATABAI:26:215-223/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r3.claim: The Prophet's duty does not extend to controlling obedience; he entrusts the outcome to God, who punishes rebels and saves faithful followers.
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r3.anchor: ليس لك من أمر طاعتهم ومعصيتهم شيء وراء ما كلفناك فكل ما وراء ذلك إلى الله

TABATABAI:26:215-223/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r4.claim: The paired divine names recall the endings of earlier stories and God's recurring pattern of punishing the disobedient while saving believers.
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r4.anchor: فهو العزيز الرحيم الذي فعل بقوم نوح وهود وصالح وإبراهيم ولوط وشعيب وقوم فرعون ما فعل

TABRISI:26:215-219/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:215-219/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:215-219/r10.claim: Entrust the matter to the mighty, who punishes enemies, and the merciful, who cares for allies, so He protects Muhammad from enemies.
TABRISI:26:215-219/r10.anchor: فوض أمرك إلى العزيز المنتقم من أعدائه الرحيم بأوليائه

THALABI:v7p183/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r4.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام
THALABI:v7p183/r4.claim: Readers in Medina and Syria read “so trust” with faʾ, as in their codices; the other readers have waw.
THALABI:v7p183/r4.anchor: فتوكل بالفاء أهل المدينة والشام وكذلك هو في مصاحفهم، وغيرهم بالواو

THALABI:v7p183/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p183/r5.claim: Trust in the Mighty, the Merciful, so that He will suffice you against your enemies' schemes.
THALABI:v7p183/r5.anchor: أي وتوكل على العزيز الرحيم ليكفيك كيد أعدائك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r1.claim: Entrust all your affairs to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: فوض إليه جميع أمرك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r2.claim: Trust God, who is mighty in punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ثق بالله {العزيز} في نقمته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r3.claim: God is merciful to them by not hastening their punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#2/r3.anchor: {الرحيم} بهم حين لم يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة

ELMALILI:26:213-223/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r7.claim: God can crush enemies and aid friends, and reliance on Him protects the Prophet from their harm.
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r7.anchor: O Azîz-i Rahîm’e, yani düşmanlarını kahra

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r4.claim: Verses 213–217 address all believers through the Prophet and direct each person to begin conveying religion to those closest to them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r4.anchor: Allah Teâlâ 213-217. âyetlerde Hz. Peygamber’in şahsında bütün müminlere hitap etmekte, dini tebliğ hususunda her müminin kendisine en yakın kimselerden başlamasını emretmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r6.claim: Because disowning rebellious relatives can cool or sour family relations, God tells leaders to disregard hostility, rely on Him, and trust His power and mercy to protect believers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r6.anchor: Bu sebeple Allah önderlerin, karşılaşacakları düşmanca davranışlara aldırış etmemelerini ve Allah’a dayanıp güvenmelerini öğütlemekte

SULAMI:v2p82#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r1.claim: Reliance is turning wholly to one's Lord and wholly away from everything besides Him, for one's need is of Him in both abodes.
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : التوكل أن تقبل بالكلية على ربك وتعرض بالكلية عما دونه بالكلية فإن إليه حاجتك في الدارين .

SULAMI:v2p82#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r2.claim: Since God is the agent and sufficient for all creation, reliance is depending on Him and finding sufficiency in Him; all else needs Him, while He is eternally self-sufficient.
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r2.anchor: سمعت عبد الله الرازي يقول : سمعت أبا عثمان يقول : التوكل مشتق من أصله ، وأصله أن الله وكيل على كل شيء والوكيل هو الله ،

SULAMI:v2p82#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r3.speaker: النهرجوري
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r3.claim: The true reliant places no burden on creation, does not complain of hardship or blame a withholder, and sees giving and withholding as from God alone.
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r3.anchor: سمعت أبا عمر بن مطر يقول : سمعت أبا بكر البردعي يقول : سمعت النهرجوري يقول : المتوكل على الحقيقة ، والصحة قد رفع مؤنته عن جميع الخلق

SULAMI:v2p82#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r4.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r4.claim: The sign of reliance is the severing of desires and expectations.
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r4.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : علامة التوكل انقطاع المطامع .

SULAMI:v2p82#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r5.speaker: أبو يزيد
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r5.claim: Abu Yazid says reliance is found whenever one truly looks for it; he also glosses it as living without attachment.
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو يزيد رحمه الله : التوكل كلما لحظته وجدته . وقال : التوكل قلت : عاش بلا علاقة .

SULAMI:v2p82#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r6.speaker: أبو يزيد
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r6.claim: Reliance is dissolving one's own planning into God's planning and accepting God as one's director.
SULAMI:v2p82#2/r6.anchor: وقال : التوكل أن تفنى تدبيرك ، في تدبيره ، وترضى بالله وكيلا مدبرا .

SAMIN-DURR:26:217/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:217/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:26:217/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-tawakkal; the faʾ makes the command a consequence of what precedes.
SAMIN-DURR:26:217/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر بالفاء. والباقون بالواو. فأما قراءة الفاء جعل فيها ما بعد الفاء

SAMIN-DURR:26:217/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:217/r2.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:26:217/r2.claim: The other readers have wa-tawakkal, merely coordinating one sentence with another.
SAMIN-DURR:26:217/r2.anchor: وقراءة الواو لمجرد عطف جملة على أخرى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p454/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p454/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p454/r6.claim: The Prophet should trust God through the coming hardships: God's might ensures none can stop His will, and His mercy will aid servants who forsake relatives for Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p454/r6.anchor: Since He is powerful, He will be able to do what He intends. None can stop Him. And since He is merciful too

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r1.claim: The life phase after acquittal is unknown and arduous; turning friends into foes is difficult, and only trust in the powerful, merciful Lord carries them through.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r1.anchor: It is not at all easy to convert friends into foes when nothing is known of the future.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p370/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p370/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p370/r1.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read فتوكل with فاء, as in the Medinan and Syrian codices; the others read with واو, as in their codices.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p370/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر: فتوكل على العزيز الرحيم [الشعراء/ 217] بالفاء، وكذلك هي في مصاحف أهل المدينة والشام.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p370/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p370/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p370/r2.claim: Al-Farisi judges both the فاء and واو readings sound.

NASHR:v2p336/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p336/r3.speaker: المدنيان، وابن عامر
NASHR:v2p336/r3.claim: The two Medinans and Ibn Amir read فتوكل with fāʾ, matching the Medinan and Syrian codices; the others read وتوكل with wāw, matching their codices.
NASHR:v2p336/r3.anchor: قرأ المدنيان، وابن عامر (فتوكل) بالفاء، وكذلك هي في مصاحف المدينة والشام

QIRAAT-ER:26:217:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:26:217:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:26:217:1#1/r1.claim: The variant fa-tawakkal uses causal fāʾ for therefore, presenting trust as a consequence; wa-tawakkal coordinates it with what precedes.
QIRAAT-ER:26:217:1#1/r1.anchor: fāʾ al-sababiyya replaces wāw al-ʿaṭf; ""therefore put your trust"" (consequence) vs

ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r1.claim: God overpowers those who disobey the Prophet through His might and supports him through His mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r1.anchor: فهو سبحانه يقهر من يعصيك منهم ومن غيرهم بعزته وينصرك برحمته

ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r2.claim: One explanation says might comes first because it best consoles the Prophet amid the people's coming hardships.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r2.anchor: وتقديم وصف العزة قيل لأنه أوفق بمقام التسلي عن المشاق اللاحقة من القوم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r3.claim: Another explanation makes might the ground that validates reliance and mercy the motive that draws one to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ذلك لأن العزة كالعلة المصححة للتوكل والرحمة كالعلة الداعية إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r4.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r4.claim: Several explain reliance as entrusting one's affair to one who owns it and can bring benefit or harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r4.anchor: وفسره غير واحد بتفويض الرجل أمره إلى من يملك أمره ويقدر على أن ينفعه ويضره

ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r5.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r5.claim: They describe the reliant person as refusing sinful self-help when a crisis strikes.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r5.anchor: وقالوا : المتوكل من إن دهمه أمر لم يحاول دفعه عن نفسه بما هو معصية لله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r6.claim: Some call that definition one of the lowest and most limited ranks of reliance.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r6.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن هذا من أحط مراتب التوكل وأدناه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r7.speaker: بعض العارفين
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r7.claim: Some gnostics distinguish three ranks: reliance with seeking and means, reliance that drops seeking and disregards means, and reliance grounded in recognizing God's prior apportionment; the highest abandons anxious scrutiny and expects no compensation.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r7.anchor: ونقل عن بعض العارفين أنه فيما بين الناس على ثلاث درجات الأولى التوكل مع الطلب ومعاطاة السبب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r8.speaker: العلامة الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r8.claim: Al-Tibi says the wording subtly signals the three ranks of reliance just described.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r8.anchor: وبين العلامة الطيبي أن في قوله تعالى : وتوكل الخ إشارة إلى المراتب الثلاث بما فيه خفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r9.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر وشيبة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r9.claim: The Medinan and Syrian codices, read by Nafi, Ibn Amir, Abu Jafar, and Shayba, have فتوكل with the conjunction fa.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r9.anchor: وفي مصاحف أهل المدينة والشام فتوكل بالفاء وبه قرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر وشيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r10.claim: The fa is parsed either as replacing the conditional response or, in al-Kashshaf, as coordination on فقل or فلا تدع; Alusi finds the first analysis more apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p136#2/r10.anchor: وجعل في الكشاف الفاء للعطف وما بعده معطوفا على ( فقل ) أو ( فلاتدع ) وما ذكر أولا أظهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r2.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r2.claim: Medina and Syria read f-tawakkal with fāʾ, as in their codices; other readers use wāw.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r2.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة، والشام: "فتوكل" بالفاء، وكذلك هو في مصاحفهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r3.claim: Trust in the Mighty and Merciful to suffice you against the enemies' schemes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r3.anchor: على العزيز الرحيم} ليكفيك كيد الأعداء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r1.claim: God can overpower His enemies and aid His allies, protecting the Prophet from harm by those who disobey him and others.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r1.anchor: الذي يقدر على قهر أعدائه ونصر أوليائه يكفك شر من يعصيك منهم ومن غيرهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read فتوكّل, substituting it as the consequence of the conditional clause.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر «فتوكل» على الإبدال من جواب الشرط.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.claim: God’s awareness of the Prophet’s deserving state follows the promise of power over enemies and support for allies, affirming reliance and reassuring his heart.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.anchor: وإنما وصفه الله تعالى بعلمه بحاله التي بها يستأهل ولايته بعد وصفه بأن من شأنه قهر أعدائه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r12.claim: Trust God for protection, deliverance, and turning those warned toward obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r12.anchor: أي في عصمتك ونجاتك والإقبال بالمنذرين إلى الطاعة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r13.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r13.claim: Medinan and Syrian readers use the causal fāʾ, which more clearly links trust to the preceding command; other readers have wāw.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r13.anchor: وقراءة أهل المدينة والشام بالفاء السببية أدل على ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r14.claim: The Mighty can protect the Prophet and take vengeance on opponents; the Merciful is hoped to honor everyone by ending discord and employing them in what pleases Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r14.anchor: أي القادر على الدفع عنكم والانتقام منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.claim: The description following the trust command establishes God’s sufficiency: His encompassing knowledge secures every benefit and repels every harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.anchor: بما يقتضي الكفاية في كل ما ينوب من دفع الضر وجلب النفع

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#3/r1.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#3/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains the command as being content with God in place of people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#3/r1.anchor: محمد بن اسحاق يعني : وتوكل على العزيز الرحيم اي : ارض به من العباد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r1.claim: Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Abu Jafar read the command with fāʾ, making trust in God follow from the disavowal in 26:216 and urging immediate refuge from the enemies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r1.anchor: قراءة نافع وابن عامر وأبي جعفر فيكون تفريعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r2.claim: The majority read with wāw, coordinating trust with the conditional answer; its connection to the condition likewise entails prompt action, so the readings yield the same result by different routes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { وتوكل } بالواو وهو عطف على جواب الشرط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r4.claim: God is sufficient for the one who trusts Him, as stated in 65:3; this supports the command to rely on Him against hostile kin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r4.anchor: ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r5.claim: The names al-Aziz and al-Rahim, the following relative clause, and the closing description signal that God attends to the Prophet's words and knows his intent; His might defeats stronger enemies and His mercy protects him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r6.claim: Tawakkul is entrusting one's affair to one who will suffice one's need; Ibn Ashur previously discussed it at 3:159.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r6.anchor: تفويض المرء أمره إلى من يكفيه مهمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر وشيبة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r1.claim: These readers and the Medinan and Syrian codices have فتوكّل with fāʾ; the other readers and codices have wa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر وشيبة «فتوكل» بالفاء وكذلك في مصاحف أهل المدينة والشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r2.claim: God orders Muḥammad to rely on Him in every matter; the attributes of might and mercy reassure him, recalling the endings of the nations' stories and God's care for each prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r2.anchor: وأمره الله تعالى بالتوكل عليه في كل أمره، ثم جاء بالصفات التي تؤنس المتوكل وهي العزة والرحمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#2/r1.claim: To rely on God is to entrust one's affair to Him; He is mighty in retribution and merciful in not hastening punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#2/r1.anchor: أي ثق به وفوض أمرك إليه فهو عزيز في نقمته رحيم لم يعجل بالعقوبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#2/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#2/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read فتوكل with an initial fāʾ; this is also the reading in the Medinan and Syrian codices.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#2/r2.anchor: وقرا نافع وابن عامر فتوكل بالفاء وكذلك هو في مصاحف أهل المدينة والشام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r1.claim: Rely on God in every affair: He supports, helps, protects, grants victory, and makes your word prevail.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r1.anchor: أي: في جميع أمورك؛ فإنه مؤيدك وناصرك وحافظك ومظفرك

JISHUMI:v7p5393/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r3.claim: Abu Ja'far and Nafi read فتوكل with fāʾ, as in Medinan codices; fāʾ stands in place of the conditional answer: if they disobey, then rely.
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع: فتوكل بالفاء وكذلك في مصاحف المدينة، الباقون بالواو

JISHUMI:v7p5393/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r4.claim: Other readers and their codices have wāw, which coordinates the command with “lower your wing.”
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r4.anchor: الباقون بالواو وكذلك في مصاحفهم. أما الفاء فهو بدل عن جواب الشرط

JISHUMI:v7p5393/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r8.claim: Tawakkul means entrusting a matter to the one who manages it.
JISHUMI:v7p5393/r8.anchor: والتوكل: تفويض الأمر إلى من يدبره.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r1.claim: Rely on God to protect you from harm by those who disobey you, from your people or elsewhere.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r1.anchor: {وتوكل } على الله يكفك شر من يعصيك منهم ومن غيرهم .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r2.claim: Tawakkul is entrusting one's affairs to the one who controls them and can bring benefit or harm.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r2.anchor: والتوكل : تفويض الرجل أمره إلى من يملك أمره ويقدر على نفعه وضره .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r3.claim: A definition says the reliant person does not try to repel a calamity through disobedience; seeking help from another person does not violate reliance if no sin is used.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r3.anchor: وقالوا : المتوكل من إن دهمه أمر لم يحاول دفعه عن نفسه بما هو معصية لله ، فعلى هذا إذا وقع الإنسان في محنة ثم سأل غيره خلاصه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r4.claim: Medinan and Syrian codices, and Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, have فتوكل.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r4.anchor: وفي مصاحف أهل المدينة والشام : ( فتوكل ) ، وبه قرأ نافع وابن عامر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r5.claim: The فاء reading can coordinate with either فقل or فلا تدع.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r5.anchor: وله محملان في العطف : أن يعطف على ( فقل ) . أو ؛ ( فلا تدع ) .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r6.claim: God is العزيز because He overpowers the Prophet's enemies, and الرحيم because He helps him against them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r6.anchor: { على العزيز الرحيم } على الذي يقهر أعداءك بعزته وينصرك عليهم برحمته .

MUQATIL:26:215-220/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:215-220/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:215-220/r3.claim: Trust means rely on God: He is mighty in retribution and merciful to them by delaying punishment.

MUQATIL:26:215-220/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:215-220/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:215-220/r4.claim: The setting is that the Prophet was invited to follow his forefathers’ religion, which Meccan unbelievers spoke about and God knows.
MUQATIL:26:215-220/r4.anchor: وذلك حين دعى إلى ملة آبائه، ثم قال سبحانه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r1.claim: God defeats the Prophet's enemies through might and helps him by mercy, shielding him from harm by those who disobey or others.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r1.anchor: على الذى يقهر أعداءك بعزته وينصرك عليهم برحمته يكفك شر من يعصيك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r2.claim: Tawakkul is entrusting one's affairs to the one who controls them and can bring benefit or harm.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r2.anchor: والتوكل تفويض الرجل أمره إلى من يملك أمره ويقدر على نفعه وضره

NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r3.claim: Some say the person who relies on God does not try to repel a crisis by disobeying Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r3.anchor: وقالوا المتوكل من إذا دهمه أمر لم يحاول دفعه عن نفسه بما هو معصية لله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r4.speaker: الجنيد
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r4.claim: Al-Junayd defines reliance as turning wholly toward God and wholly away from all else, since one's need is for Him in both abodes.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r4.anchor: وقال الجنيدر رضى الله عنه التوكل ان تقبل بالكلية على ربك وتعرض بالكلية عما دونه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r5.speaker: مدني وشامي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r5.claim: Madinan and Shami read fa-tawakkal; it is coordinated either with fa-qul or with fa-lā tadʿu.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#9/r5.anchor: فتوكل مدنى وشامى عطف على فقل أو فلا تدع

QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r9.claim: Entrust affairs to God: He cannot be overcome and, in His mercy, does not abandon His allies.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r9.anchor: { وتوكل على العزيز الرحيم } أي فوض أمرك إليه فإنه العزيز الذي لا يغالب، الرحيم الذي لا يخذل أولياءه

QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r10.claim: The common reading has wāw, as in their codices; Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read with fāʾ, as in the Medinan and Syrian codices.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r10.anchor: وقرأ العامة: { وتوكل } بالواو وكذلك هو في مصاحفهم. وقرأ نافع وابن عامر «فتوكل» بالفاء وكذلك هو في مصاحف المدينة والشام
